title: Loop card
description: The frontmatter of loops/<id>/card.md: the one description of a loop that the plugin and the site read. scripts/catalog.py check validates every card against it, and checks what a schema cannot say: the id is the folder's name, the sections, the speed range, the places against the super-loops' phases, the related ids, the image.
$comment: catalog.py implements the subset of JSON Schema used here: $ref to $defs, type, const, enum, oneOf, not, if/then/else, properties, required, additionalProperties: false, items, minItems, maxItems, uniqueItems, minLength, maxLength, pattern, format: uri. Keep to it, or extend catalog.py.

id.description: The name of the card's folder. Stable: links, the site's address and the plugin refer to it.

title.description: The loop's name, as a card shows it. The explanation goes in summary.

summary.description: What the loop does, in one line: what the agent does and what signal it gets. The list of loops on the site and the agent choosing loops read only this.

image.description: Optional: an illustration, a file in the card's folder.

sensor.description: What gives the loop's signal. It decides how far the signal can be trusted.

oneOf.description: A program: tests, a linter, a compiler, a query. Deterministic and cheap; it may block at once.
An LLM agent: a review, a verdict, a grade. Not deterministic; it blocks only once calibrated (agent-calibration).
A person: the only sensor of intent, slow and costly. Such a loop has the axes when, initiator, sync and assesses.

ilities.description: The quality attributes the loop checks, the main one first.

places.description: Where the loop serves in the super-loops: <super-loop>/<phase>, or harness:<super-loop>/<phase> at the harness level. The super-loop must have the phase: discovery has no release.

speed.description: How long one round takes: one value, or a range [from, to], the faster first.

needs.description: What the agent must reach from its session beyond the repository; [] when nothing. The values are the keys of tools in a project's profile, so the plugin can tell which loops a project can run.

agent.description: Optional: the kinds of agent that are a step of the loop. A card with this field has an Agent step section.

related.description: Optional: the ids of loops that pair with this one.

links.description: Where to read more: the sources of the card. [] when it has none yet, and its Notes say so.

oneOf.description: Before the work.
During the work.
After the work.
In production.

when.description: Human loops: when the person is in the loop. The earlier, the cheaper a misunderstanding is to fix.

initiator.description: Human loops: who starts the loop.

oneOf.description: The agent asks.
A person interrupts.
A gate by rule.
A schedule.

sync.description: Human loops: whether the agent waits for the person.

oneOf.description: The agent waits.
The agent goes on.
What is wanted.
How the agent will do it.
What the agent made.
The change itself.
Whether an action is safe to take.

assesses.description: Human loops: what the person assesses.

human-only.description: only a loop with sensor: human has this axis

oneOf.description: The product does what it was specified to do: functional suitability, completeness, faultlessness.
The work is what the person meant: the intent, the plan and the result match what was wanted.
Behaviour can be checked by tests, and the tests catch what they should.
The code is easy to read, change and extend: modularity, analysability, modifiability, evolvability, understandability.
Confidentiality, integrity, privacy, compliance, audit and licences.
It works with other systems, versions, platforms and locales: integrability, interoperability, portability, i18n.
Time behaviour, resource use, capacity, scalability.
Availability, fault tolerance, recoverability, resilience.
What the system does can be seen and explained: logs, metrics, traces, debuggability, operability.
A change reaches where it runs, reproducibly and safely: builds, environments, rollouts, installability.
People can use it: accessibility, UX, interaction.
After every file edit: a hook, the language server.
The agent runs it in its own workspace.
A pre-commit or pre-push hook.
CI on clean infrastructure.
A per-PR preview environment.
Staging.
Production.
On a schedule: nightly, periodically, in batches.
Within a task or session: at its start, at its end, or when something in it calls for it.
Once per sprint.
All the time.

speed.description: From the fastest to the slowest.

oneOf.description: CI status and logs: gh, glab, a CI MCP server.
Logs: Elasticsearch, Loki, Datadog, CloudWatch.
Error tracking: Sentry, Bugsnag, Crashlytics.
Metrics: Prometheus, Grafana.
Traces: an OpenTelemetry backend.
A browser or a simulator: Playwright, Chrome DevTools MCP, iOS Simulator, adb.
Deploys to a stand: kubectl, helm, the Vercel CLI, a CI job the agent can start.
Reads a diff or an artifact through a lens or a checklist, returns findings. Blocks only once calibrated.
Tries to prove a claim of done wrong, by running tests and opening the app. Blocks only once calibrated.
Grades a result on a rubric. Blocks only once calibrated on a person's grades.
Walks the running app like a user, returns what it saw and the defects. Does not block: what it finds becomes a test.
Reads logs, traces, profiles or a CI log, returns a diagnosis. Does not block: it helps the working agent.
Does a narrow task on a schedule, returns a small PR. Does not block: the loops on its PR decide.

title.description: The title of the article, book or talk.

url.description: Its address; a book may have none.

author.description: Who wrote it: a person or an organisation.

note.description: What the card takes from it, when that is not plain from the title.
